procedure.name: Firewall Log Analysis
procedure.description: The Defenders analyze logs generated by the firewall to monitor network traffic patterns, detect unauthorized access, and identify anomalies such as unusual connections or high traffic volumes.

procedure.name: Network Threat Hunting
procedure.description: The Defenders analyze network traffic to actively hunt for signs of malicious activity, such as unusual protocols, C2 communication, or data exfil.

procedure.name: Active Defense and Cyber Deception
procedure.description: The Defenders simulate real systems and services, luring attackers to interact with them, carefully monitoring and alerting on those interactions.

procedure.name: Endpoint Security Protection Analysis
procedure.description: The Defenders deploy and monitor endpoint security solutions to detect and prevent unauthorized access and activity on endpoints.

procedure.name: User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA)
procedure.description: The Defenders leverage advanced analytics to detect anomalies in user behavior, identifying potential insider threats, compromised accounts, or unusual activity patterns.

procedure.name: Endpoint Analysis
procedure.description: The Defenders investigate endpoint devices to identify indicators of compromise, unauthorized changes, or suspicious activities.

procedure.name: Isolation
procedure.description: The Defenders quarantine compromised systems or network segments to prevent further spread of malicious activity, containing threats while enabling secure investigation and remediation.

procedure.name: Crisis Management
procedure.description: The Defenders coordinate response efforts during cybersecurity incidents, ensuring effective communication and swift containment.

procedure.name: Memory Analysis
procedure.description: The Defenders pull the memory from the suspect system and review it for possible malicious activity, such as running malware, hidden processes, or unauthorized code execution.

procedure.name: Cloud Event Log Analysis
procedure.description: The Defenders monitor, collect, and examine event logs generated by cloud-based systems and services to identify potential security incidents, misconfigurations, and unusual or unauthorized activities.

procedure.name: Permissions Audit
procedure.description: The Defenders examine configurations such as Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles in Microsoft Active Directory, Amazon Web Services (AWS), Azure AD permissions, or file access controls to detect excessive privileges, unauthorized access, or potential insider threats.

procedure.name: Cloud Event Log Analysis
procedure.description: Are you missing what should be in your cloud logs? Do you even know what cloud provider logs you need in an incident response situation? There are thousands of data connectors in your cloud service provider. Have any of them changed since the last time you reviewed them? Good luck hunting for a specific needle in a stack of needles.
tools: Check with your cloud provider and see what tools they provide. It's ok, you're paying them a ton of money for all this.

procedure.name: Permissions Audit
procedure.description: Users can have everything by default... which makes your organization vulnerable by design. Who gets to do what and why? Who is the magical unicorn that gets the exceptions? Are permissions open for convenience? When was the last time you fixed something a security audit didn't make you do? You can be the decider if you want--the power is yours!

inject.name: False Alarm: It Was a Penetration Test
inject.description: Relax, it wasn't an APT, or any T for that matter — It was the External Pentesting firm the Defenders' CEO hired. They've breached everything, and now the Defenders are paying them to be told how bad it was. The Incident Captain ends the session and the Defenders discuss how they would have detected the Attack Techniques and Procedures of the Penetration Testers.

inject.name: Data Uploaded to Pastebin
inject.description: Surprise! The attackers spilled sensitive customer data all over Pastebin. Now customers are learning about the breach over their morning coffee... from The News. The Defenders must play their Crisis Management Detection. If they are successful, they can move past this issue. If they aren't, they receive a -2 modifier on all Detections for the rest of the session.

inject.name: Analyst Returns from Incident Response Training
inject.description: Armed with newfound Splunk-fu, the Defenders' Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) analyst is now a log-sifting ninja. Attackers, beware! The regex game just leveled up. The Defenders get a +2 modifier for all Detections until the end of the session.

inject.name: Policy? What Policy?
inject.description: Oops, that Detection just vanished faster than the Defenders' budget during Q4. Good luck explaining this one! The Incident Captain must remove a Detection Card.

inject.name: Luck of The SOC
inject.description: Congrats! The Defenders hit the Detection Roulette Jackpot. Let's hope it's more useful than a phishing awareness poster. The Incident Captain must reveal one of the Attack Cards.

inject.name: Bobby the Intern Kills the System You are Reviewing
inject.description: In a bold move of intern ingenuity, Bobby decides "reboot" means "unplug everything." The Defenders' investigation is now as dead as the server. The Defenders lose their next turn.

inject.name: Legal takes Your Most Skilled Handler into a Meeting to Explain the Incident
inject.description: Who brought a lawyer to the party? There's always one person who pretty much runs the whole IR process — that "One Essential Person." Well, the legal team just took that person away for "Very Important Reasons." The Defenders lose the +3 modifier on Established Detections for 2 turns.

inject.name: Crank Up the Pressure
inject.description: The attackers have started contacting your clients stating that they have compromised personally identifiable information (PII) and your company was not willing to protect it. Word spreads quickly on social media.
inject.notes: Leadership is demanding results faster than you can possibly deliver, the Defenders lose 1 turn.

inject.name: Communication Infrastucture DDoS
inject.description: An attack group unrelated to the current scenario runs a DDoS attack against your communications infrastructure during the incident.
inject.notes: The Defenders must use an alternative form of communication for the next two turns.

inject.name: Way to Plan Ahead
inject.description: The security team brought on DenSecure™ for threat emulation against known threat actor behavior. The team has implemented new detections that caught the attacker's persistence actions within the network.
inject.notes: The Incident Captain must reveal the Persistence card.

inject.name: Water, Water Everywhere!
inject.description: A pipe bursts in the server room. Seems like a good time to model that new flower print bathing suit while the backup site is brought online.
inject.notes: The Defenders receive a -3 modifier for the next two turns.

inject.name: Timber!
inject.description: A tree falls and knocks out power to your office -- time to head to a secondary location. Unfortunately, traffic is terrible and you'll be stuck in the car for a while.
inject.notes: The Defender who rolled the die and caused this Inject can't help the team for three turns while they're stuck in traffic.

inject.name: It's a Feature, not a Bug
inject.description: A penetration test reveals a critical severity issue in one of your core technologies that the vendor claims is a feature, not a bug. The Defenders implement their own defenses to mitigate exploitation.
inject.notes: The Defenders receive a +2 modifier on all Procedure cards for the rest of the session.

inject.name: Dude...Where's My Server?
inject.description: Your organization's users contact the helpdesk saying all of their fileshares are missing. Security footage reveals an unknown person absconding with the physical drives.
inject.notes: Server Analysis is unavailable to the Defenders for the rest of the session -- in addition, they lose 1 turn as they figure out whose problem this is.

inject.name: Executive Buy-In
inject.description: An at-home PC compromise has your CEO's personally identifiable information (PII) all over the web. Suddenly, management cares a lot about security and has approved all of the team's training requests.
inject.notes: The Defenders receive a +2 modifier on all Procedure cards for the rest of the session.

initial.name: Missing HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) Protection

initial.description: The attackers insert malware in the update process of one of your key enterprise management tools. This gives them direct access to the heart of your infrastructure.

pivot.name: Access Token Manipulation

pivot.name: Stale Network Address Configurations (SNAC) Attack
pivot.description: The attackers take advantage of a system or a network service that has been configured with a hard-coded IP address or fully qualified domain name (FQDN) that is no longer associated with a live host.

pivot.name: Cleartext Passwords in Files
pivot.description: The attackers love people who share and save passwords in files everyone else can read. This attack works because people (often admins and developers) create documents and spreadsheets with passwords in them. Then, they put them on shares that are readable to everyone in the domain.

persist.description: The attackers' malware triggers only when specific events occur. For example, when a specific DLL or service is started.

persist.name: Malware Injection into Client Software
persist.description: The attackers insert their malware to run alongside (or in) third-party software. Stuxnet and Bonadan did this.

persist.name: Malicious Email Rules
persist.description: The attackers create rules in an email inbox and/or client that trigger on specific events or when certain keywords are present in a message.

persist.name: Windows Service Recovery Actions

inject.name: SIEM Goes Down

inject.name: This Isn't the First Time, and Won't Be the Last

inject.name: Attackers Taunt You

inject.name: No Good Deed Goes Unpunished...

inject.name: Our Friend “Hacky”

inject.notes: Have the Incident Master draw an additional Initial Compromise Card.

inject.name: Is It Getting Hot in Here?

inject.name: "Don't Forget to Smash the Subscribe Button!"

detection: Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) Log Analysis

persist.name: Malicious Browser Plugins

persist.name: Logon Scripts

persist.name: Malicious Firmware

persist.name: Accessibility Features

persist.name: Living Off The Land

persist.name: Hiding in Plain Sight

persist.name: Registry Modification

persist.name: WMI Events

detection: Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) Log Analysis

procedure.name: Server Analysis
procedure.description: The Defenders monitor server activity, logs, and configurations to detect abnormal behaviors, such as unauthorized access, unusual traffic, or process anomalies.

procedure.name: Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) Log Analysis
procedure.description: The Defenders use SIEM to aggregate logs from systems and devices to identify abnormal patterns, such as unusual access, traffic, or attack signatures.

procedure.name: Firewall Log Analysis
procedure.description: The Defenders analyze logs generated by the firewall to monitor network traffic patterns, detect unauthorized access, and identify anomalies such as unusual connections or high traffic volumes.

procedure.name: Network Threat Hunting
procedure.description: The Defenders analyze network traffic to actively hunt for signs of malicious activity, such as unusual protocols, C2 communication, or data exfil.

procedure.name: Active Defense and Cyber Deception
procedure.description: The Defenders simulate real systems and services, luring attackers to interact with them, carefully monitoring and alerting on those interactions.

procedure.name: Endpoint Security Protection Analysis
procedure.description: The Defenders deploy and monitor endpoint security solutions to detect and prevent unauthorized access and activity on endpoints.

procedure.name: User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA)
procedure.description: The Defenders leverage advanced analytics to detect anomalies in user behavior, identifying potential insider threats, compromised accounts, or unusual activity patterns.

procedure.name: Endpoint Analysis
procedure.description: The Defenders investigate endpoint devices to identify indicators of compromise, unauthorized changes, or suspicious activities.

procedure.name: Isolation
procedure.description: The Defenders quarantine compromised systems or network segments to prevent further spread of malicious activity, containing threats while enabling secure investigation and remediation.

procedure.name: Crisis Management
procedure.description: The Defenders coordinate response efforts during cybersecurity incidents, ensuring effective communication and swift containment.

procedure.name: Memory Analysis
procedure.description: The Defenders pull the memory from the suspect system and review it for possible malicious activity, such as running malware, hidden processes, or unauthorized code execution.

procedure.name: Cloud Event Log Analysis
procedure.description: The Defenders monitor, collect, and examine event logs generated by cloud-based systems and services to identify potential security incidents, misconfigurations, and unusual or unauthorized activities.

procedure.name: Permissions Audit
procedure.description: The Defenders examine configurations such as Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles in Microsoft Active Directory, Amazon Web Services (AWS), Azure AD permissions, or file access controls to detect excessive privileges, unauthorized access, or potential insider threats.

procedure.name: Sequence of Events (SOE) Analysis
procedure.description: Reviewing the data historian and sequence of events (SOE) recordings can determine which part of the process showed signs of impact, during what time period this occurred, and in what order.

procedure.name: Protocol Analysis
procedure.description: Examining the protocol traffic on a network can determine what systems should be talking and what systems shouldn't be talking to each other on specific protocols.

procedure.name: Crisis Management
procedure.description: Your legal and management teams have procedures to minimize the risk to human safety and property loss while preparing communica- tion for external stakeholders. A good notification strategy will help deal with any crisis.

procedure.name: Site Walkthrough
procedure.description: Sending personnel to the site to examine the written logs, look for wireless access points, physical ingress methods, and equipment stacks can help identify abnormalities.

procedure.name: Shodan Review
procedure.description: Our ICS equipment shouldn't be visible directly from the internet, but stuff happens. By looking for hostnames, certificates, keywords, and other fingerprints, we find "air-gapped" systems enumerated in Shodan.

procedure.name: Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) Log Analysis
procedure.description: Yeah... good luck with this one. Are you logging the right things? Do you regularly emulate attack scenarios to see if you can detect them?

procedure.name: Firewall Log Review
procedure.description: Can your organization analyze and understand firewall logs? Do you regularly emulate attack scenarios and verify that your procedures work?

procedure.name: Consequence-Driven Threat Hunting
procedure.description: Does your team consider their worst industrial consequences, track down what systems could cause those hazards, what mitigations are in place, and use those to map attacker tools, tactics, and procedures to hypothesize and hunt for malicious activity?

procedure.name: Employee Interviews
procedure.description: Your team gets to interview the operators, architects, vendors, and security personnel at the site of the incident.

procedure.name: User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA)
procedure.description: It's like logging, but it actually works. User and entity behavior analytics (UEBA) looks for multiple concurrent logons, impossible logons based on geography, unusual file access, password sprays, and more!

procedure.name: Endpoint Analysis
procedure.description: This is where the Defenders use their SANS IR Cheat Sheets to detect attacks on workstations. Time to bring in the Local Operator... and pray.

procedure.name: Memory Analysis
procedure.description: The Defenders pull the memory from the suspect system and review it for possible malicious activity.

inject.name: Unexpected PLC State Change
inject.description: A programmable logic controller (PLC) has exhibited an unexpected start/stop state change. This indicates the attackers are currently active.
inject.notes: The Defenders gain a +2 modifier for Protocol Analysis on their next turn for knowing where to look.

inject.name: Safety Instrumented System (SIS) Tampering
inject.description: A safety instrumented system (SIS) goes offline, and when the maintenance crew examines it, the firmware checksum does not match.
inject.notes: The Defenders receive a +2 modifier for Endpoint Analysis on their next turn for knowing where to look.

inject.name: Mediation
inject.description: The Defenders have to function as mediators between the IT and ICS network teams.
inject.notes: All future turns receive a -1 modifier until they reveal an Attack Card, then all turns thereafter receive a +1 modifier for the goodwill period.

inject.name: You Can't Get There From Here
inject.description: Due to the remote location and travel logistics, the Defenders have to walk a site operator through the evidence collection process.
inject.notes: They receive a -1 modifier on Endpoint Analysis and Memory Analysis for the rest of the session.

inject.name: Emergency Facility Shutdown
inject.description: A compromise of a hazardous material container causes an immediate evacuation of the production facility. This is where all of the backbone ICS routers are located.
inject.notes: The Defenders lose 1 turn.

inject.name: Legacy Knowledge
inject.description: The Defenders must roll again to see if the person who built the system is still working at the site.
inject.notes: (1-10) means the happily retired individual is not there to assist them. -2 modifier on the next turn (11-20) means the grizzled veteran that deployed the legacy system still works at the site to assist them. +2 modifier on the next turn

inject.name: No High Availability (HA) System
inject.description: Current endpoint investigations are on fragile systems that are without redundancy.
inject.notes: The Defenders are limited to collecting information with the tools already installed. They receive a -2 modifier on Endpoint Analysis and Memory Analysis for the next two turns.

inject.name: No Shirt, No Shoes
inject.description: Half of the Defenders have been deemed to be wearing inadequate personal protective equipment (PPE). They may not enter the site until they purchase full leather uppers and cotton clothes.
inject.notes: The Defenders may elect to receive a -4 modifier on their next turn OR lose 1 turn and receive a +4 modifier on the turn thereafter.

inject.name: USB Worm
inject.description: The USB devices used for collecting information become infected with Autorun malware.
inject.notes: The Defenders receive a -2 modifier on Endpoint Analysis and Memory Analysis for the next two turns.

They've breached everything, and now the Defenders are paying them to be told how bad it was. The Incident Captain ends the session and the Defenders discuss how they would have detected the Attack Techniques and Procedures of the Penetration Testers.

inject.name: Data Uploaded to Pastebin
inject.description: Surprise! The attackers spilled sensitive customer data all over Pastebin. Now customers are learning about the breach over their morning coffee... from The News. The Defenders must play their Crisis Management Detection. If they are successful, they can move past this issue. If they aren't, they receive a -2 modifier on all Detections for the rest of the session.

inject.name: Analyst Returns from Incident Response Training
inject.description: Armed with newfound Splunk-fu, the Defenders' Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) analyst is now a log-sifting ninja. Attackers, beware! The regex game just leveled up. The Defenders get a +2 modifier for all Detections until the end of the session.

inject.name: Policy? What Policy?
inject.description: Oops, that Detection just vanished faster than the Defenders' budget during Q4. Good luck explaining this one! The Incident Captain must remove a Detection Card.

inject.name: Luck of The SOC
inject.description: Congrats! The Defenders hit the Detection Roulette Jackpot. Let's hope it's more useful than a phishing awareness poster. The Incident Captain must reveal one of the Attack Cards.

inject.name: Bobby the Intern Kills the System You are Reviewing
inject.description: In a bold move of intern ingenuity, Bobby decides "reboot" means "unplug everything." The Defenders' investigation is now as dead as the server. The Defenders lose their next turn.

inject.name: Legal takes Your Most Skilled Handler into a Meeting to Explain the Incident
inject.description: Who brought a lawyer to the party? There's always one person who pretty much runs the whole IR process — that "One Essential Person." Well, the legal team just took that person away for "Very Important Reasons." The Defenders lose the +3 modifier on Established Detections for 2 turns.

inject.name: AI Hacked Into Your Cloud Accounts
inject.description: You offended the sentient AI because you thought it was funny to tease it.
inject.notes: Ask your AI chatbot of choice to determine if your Procedures work or not. No more die-rolling for your team. AI has your job now. AI is now overlord. Long live AI.

inject.name: Cloud Provider Disabled Vulnerable Functionality
inject.description: Your cloud provider disabled old legacy protocols, thereby making authentication to your environment more secure. Less attack surface is good, but it means that you have to ensure that legacy applications and functions are still working correctly.
inject.notes: The Defenders receive a +2 modifier on all cloud-related Procedures for the rest of the session.

inject.name: Cloud Bill Due
inject.description: It's time to pay up for your cloud provider services. You find that someone left too many resources running, resulting in sky-high costs.
inject.notes: The Defenders lose capital in their budget. To determine how much they've lost, they must roll a D20: (1-10) means the team must decide which (2) Procedure Cards to disable for the next three turns. (11-20) means the team must decide which (1) Procedure Card to disable for the next two turns.

inject.name: Security Awareness Training for the Win!
inject.description: The Defenders had Security Awareness Training set up for the employees. This raised the general security posture of the organization. Good job!
inject.notes: The Defenders receive a +3 modifier for the next three turns.

inject.name: Cloud Security Training
inject.description: The Defenders attended cloud security training, where they learned about the latest threats to cloud environments.
inject.notes: Yay! You're taking active steps to better your team. This has helped your organization understand threats and defend your assets better. The Incident Captain must reveal any attack card that is cloud related.

inject.name: Ignore Those Pesky Open Ports
inject.description: A server has Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) exposed on the internet and nobody checked Huntress External Recon to identify this threat. A new attacker has come in during the middle of the incident.
inject.notes: The Incident Captain draws an additional Initial Compromise card.

inject.name: A Bad Day Made Worse
inject.description: The Threat Research team at Huntress discloses a zero-day vulnerability in the Defenders' business-critical software package and it must be addressed immediately.
inject.notes: The Defenders lose 1 turn.

inject.name: Cryptominer
inject.description: The attackers have compromised your cloud account and spun up hundreds of virtual machines with cryptominers running on them. You're lucky that's all they did... or is it?
inject.notes: The Defenders lose capital in their budget and must decide as a team which Procedure Card to disable for the rest of the session.

inject.name: Dangling Domains
inject.description: One of your domains has been hijacked to host malware because a DNS entry was not removed after deleting a resource that it was pointed at. Your website is spewing malware to all visitors.
inject.notes: The Defenders must play their Crisis Management procedure. If they are successful, they can move past this issue. If they aren't, they lose their most senior incident handler for the rest of the session as they speak to "management."

inject.name: Haste Makes Waste
inject.description: The Defenders didn't consult their cyber insurance provider before starting the incident response (IR) plan. Remediation efforts are delayed while the preferred IR vendor is brought up to speed.
inject.notes: The Defenders lose 1 turn and must explain how they will proceed.

inject.name: Alert Fatigue is Real
inject.description: The Defenders' endpoint detection and response (EDR) solution was not managed.
inject.notes: The Defenders receive a -3 modifier on Endpoint Security Protection Analysis for the rest of the session.

inject.name: Exposed Cloud Access Keys During Public Presentation
inject.description: One of your IT staff just gave an amazing presentation demoing an epic new open-source tool but forgot to redact live cloud access keys. Members of the audience quickly logged in and accessed your company resources.
inject.notes: Accidents happen, but what do you do when someone exposes your organization inadvertently? The Incident Captain must draw an additional Pivot and Escalate card.

inject.name: Food Poisoning
inject.description: The life of this organization depends upon just one thing: finding someone back there who can not only work this incident, but who didn't have fish for dinner.
inject.notes: Each of the Defenders must roll a D20 and the person with the lowest number will finish the session by themselves without any assistance from the others.

inject.name: I'm Not the Cloud Person
inject.description: No one on your staff knows anything about cloud security. Seriously, you faked your resumes.
inject.notes: Each of the Defenders must roll a D20 and the person with the lowest number will handle the next three turns by themselves while the others study up on cloud security.

inject.name: Knowledge is Power
inject.description: The Defenders attended a recent Huntress Tradecraft Tuesday episode about "Quick Forensics for the Lazy Investigator." This taught the Defenders the latest persistence techniques used by attackers.
inject.notes: The Incident Captain must reveal the Persistence card.

inject.name: SIEM Goes Down
inject.description: No SIEM for you!
inject.notes: It is discovered that due to an intern error, your logging server/SIEM has not been logging properly for the last two weeks. All SIEM actions are off the table for the rest of the session.

inject.name: Regional Cloud Provider Data Center Outage
inject.description: Cloud providers use specific geographic regions to group real-world devices in datacenters. The region where your cloud resources are located is currently undergoing an unplanned outage. No cloud for you!
inject.notes: Cloud Event Log Analysis and Permissions Audit procedures are unavailable for the next three turns.

inject.name: That Was a Bad Idea
inject.description: The host isolation feature in the Huntress platform was disabled by the Defenders, allowing the attackers to move freely through the environment.
inject.notes: The Incident Captain draws an additional Pivot and Escalate card.

inject.name: This Isn't the First Time, and Won't Be the Last
inject.description: This is not the first time the attackers have been on your network.
inject.notes: Through forensic analysis, it has been discovered that the backdoor had internal DNS servers’ IP addresses hard-coded in them because the attackers have been in before. Have the Incident Captain draw an additional Persistence Card.

inject.name: EDR Compromise
inject.description: The attackers gain access to your Endpoint Protection suite of tools.
inject.notes: Endpoints stop reporting to the EDR console… The attackers found a console session that hadn’t timed out yet and issued mass uninstalls. All Endpoint Security Protection Analysis actions are unavailable for the rest of the session.

inject.name: Read to The End
inject.description: The Defenders neglected to perform a root cause analysis (RCA) and the attackers easily regain control.
inject.notes: The Incident Captain draws an additional Persistence card.

inject.name: Third-Party Code Library Compromised
inject.description: Your favorite infosec podcast (BHIS?) reported that your source code contains a third-party library that has been compromised to include malware. Since you have included this library as a dependency in your code, it is now running malicious commands on systems where it is implemented.
inject.notes: The Defenders must play their Crisis Management procedure. If they are successful, they can move past this issue. If they aren't, they receive a -2 modifier on all procedures for the rest of the session.

inject.name: Attackers Taunt You
inject.description: The attackers call out the security team, via a message to every system on the network.
inject.notes: The attackers use msg command to send a pop-up to incident responders, "Shall we play a game?"

inject.name: Back to Basics
inject.description: The Defenders configured their monitoring tools to alert when security tools stop working. The attackers disabled the endpoint detection and response (EDR) solution and the Defenders were alerted immediately.
inject.notes: The Defenders receive a +3 modifier on Endpoint Security Protection Analysis for the next time it's used.

inject.name: Attackers Timestomp Key Evidence Files
inject.description: (-3) Modifier for Log-Related Actions There are tools that allow attackers to modify Modified-Accessed-Created-Entry (MACE) timestamps of files. One such tool is in Metasploit called Timestomp.
inject.notes: The attackers can change the MACE for their malware to be in the future. What does this do to your handling of evidence? Can you trust timestamps at all?

inject.name: Bear vs. Powerstation
inject.description: A bear attacked the power substation for your datacenter. Don't worry, he's down, but so is your datacenter. The only thing worse than the smell is not having a hot backup facility.
inject.notes: The defenders lose 1 turn as they discuss the difference between a hot backup and a cold backup.

inject.name: Rookie Mistake
inject.description: An entry-level tech neglected to read an incident report that instructed them to block a known C2 server IP address at the firewall. Dammit, Bobby!
inject.notes: The Incident Captain draws an additional C2 and Exfil card.

inject.name: A Little Help From My Friends
inject.description: The Defenders have been investing time and resources into cybersecurity peer groups, developing relationships with fellow professionals to help each other in times of need.
inject.notes: The Defenders draw a Consultant card of their choosing.

inject.name: Ghosted by AV
inject.description: A recent unverified update caused all endpoints to alarm on false positives. A useless antivirus is as good as no AV at all. Do you shut it down or keep it running while sifting through all the noise?
inject.notes: The Defenders receive a -3 modifier on Endpoint Security Protection Analysis for the rest of the session.

inject.name: Missed Payday
inject.description: The attackers compromise your email account, email HR, and instruct them to update your direct deposit information, routing your paycheck into a bank account they control.
inject.notes: Each of the Defenders must roll a D20 and the person with the lowest number has to get a night job as a bartender and must remain silent for the rest of the session.

inject.name: No Good Deed Goes Unpunished...
inject.description: The Purple Team uncovers another incident.
inject.notes: When tuning your detection capabilities during a purple team engagement (unrelated to the incident at hand), your team detects another attack. You now have two compromises to deal with. Have the Incident Captain pull another set of Attack Cards. The Defenders get five extra turns.

inject.name: DiscountConsultant.lol
inject.description: Ever since hiring Scott, this incident response has gone from bad to worse. He had us chasing the wrong lead the whole time. Turns out, our consultant has no real IR experience despite a senior title. Luckily, he has red team experience and recognizes the TTPs.
inject.notes: The Defenders must roll a die. If the die is even, the Incident Captain must reveal the Initial Compromise card. If the die is odd, the Incident Captain must draw another Persistence card.

inject.name: Not a Red Team
inject.description: The network threat-hunting team has detected C2 beacons on multiple machines in your environment. The attackers can now install additional payloads on the affected machines.
inject.notes: Have the Incident Captain draw an additional Persistence Card as well as a Pivot and Escalate Card.

inject.name: Our Friend, Hacky
inject.description: You discover other attackers have been on your network for months.
inject.notes: Have the Incident Captain draw an additional Initial Compromise Card.

inject.name: Risk Accepted
inject.description: Turns out the endpoint detection and response (EDR) solution was only installed on "business critical" servers. Management wouldn't approve the cost of covering all devices.
inject.notes: Endpoint Security Protection Analysis is unavailable for the rest of the session.

inject.name: Deez Registry Keyz Plz?
inject.description: A wild malicious registry key appears. The bad news: It is on 50 endpoints that are now rampant with malware. The good news: Management cares.
inject.notes: The Defenders get 3 additional turns to help solve the incident and a Consultant Card of their choice without rolling a D20.

inject.name: Is it Getting Hot in Here?
inject.description: HVAC systems are important... and they will fail at the worst times. This... is one of those times.
inject.notes: Your data center HVAC system is infected with a worm. It’s supposed to be air-gapped. It is 103°F outside, and the server temperatures are rising. All servers need to be shut down. RIGHT NOW! Hope you have a "hot site."

inject.name: Major Failure Alert
inject.description: The Defenders disabled multi-factor authentication (MFA) for a third-party vendor's service account to access the internal network. This allows attackers to spread further throughout the organization.
inject.notes: The Incident Captain draws an additional Pivot and Escalate card AND Persistence card.

inject.name: Trimarc123!
inject.description: The attackers' access to your network just fell into their laps. The local admin account on all workstations share the same password, so if the attackers gained admin on one workstation, they can now log in to them all.
inject.notes: If one of the Defenders can accurately explain LAPS, the Incident Captain must reveal the Pivot & Escalate card. Otherwise, the Incident Captain must draw an additional Pivot & Escalate card.

inject.name: Crank Up the Pressure
inject.description: The attackers have started contacting your clients stating that they have compromised personally identifiable information (PII) and your company was not willing to protect it. Word spreads quickly on social media.
inject.notes: Leadership is demanding results faster than you can possibly deliver, the Defenders lose 1 turn.

inject.name: Don't Forget to Smash the Subscribe Button!
inject.description: Some attackers just want to watch the world burn.
inject.notes: The attackers post a YouTube video detailing the extent of their attack because it wasn't getting the press they thought it deserved.

inject.name: Dude, Where's Our Docs?
inject.description: The project to fully document important incident response procedures was not started on time and never finished.
inject.notes: The Defenders no longer have a +3 modifier on their Established Procedure cards.

inject.name: Let's Rock
inject.description: The Defenders' Lead Incident Responder decides to reinvent themselves as a rock musician and goes on tour.
inject.notes: All procedures receive a -1 modifier for the rest of the session.

inject.name: Nuclear Test Site
inject.description: Thank goodness the Defenders are Atomic Red Team™ power users and they are prepared for all the endpoint threats.
inject.notes: The Defenders receive a +2 modifier on Endpoint Analysis and Endpoint Security Protection Analysis for the rest of the session.

inject.name: Click, Click, Boom
inject.description: Instead of buying new hard drives, you decided to save some money on "refurbished" drives. Don't worry, you didn't use those drives on anything important -- only your SIEM -- ya know, that system you spend all that money on and don't use.
inject.notes: SIEM Log Analysis is unavailable to the Defenders for the rest of the session.

inject.name: Communication Infrastucture DDoS
inject.description: An attack group unrelated to the current scenario runs a DDoS attack against your communications infrastructure during the incident.
inject.notes: The Defenders must use an alternative form of communication for the next two turns.

inject.name: Quishing
inject.description: The local burger joint uses a QR code for its menu. How convenient! Unfortunately, a disgruntled ex-analyst knows the Defenders are regulars and put a malicious QR code over the legitimate one. Anyone who scanned it compromised their MFA device, which now needs to be wiped or replaced.
inject.notes: The Endpoint Security Protection Analysis card is unavailable for the next two turns.

inject.name: Undocumented Application Programming Interfaces (API)
inject.description: The attackers have performed their actions using undocumented cloud provider APIs, and none of their activity is showing up in your SIEM solution. Your Cloud SIEM can no longer trust the data coming from your cloud provider. The Cloud Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) Log Analysis Detection is unavailable for the next 3 turns.

inject.name: Attacker Stops Cloud Logging
inject.description: The attackers stop control plane logging altogether, making the security team blind to future attacker behavior. Choose one Defender to skip 2 turns while they deal with the high-severity incident.

inject.name: Cat on Keyboard Deletes Production Database
inject.description: Curiosity killed the database entries! A work-from-home administrator left their computer unlocked and, in an attempt to gain additional snuggles, their cat happened to spam out a mass delete on their keyboard. Oops.
inject.notes: Each of the Defenders must roll a D20. The first two people to roll an odd number have to go fix the database and must remain silent for the rest of the session. Even number rollers move on to finish the incident.

inject.name: Peekaboo
inject.description: Remember that DIY security camera you set up to keep an eye on your servers? Well, you forgot to secure it and change the default password, so now the bad guys know all of your secrets.
inject.notes: The Incident Captain must draw an additional Initial Compromise card.

inject.name: Way to Plan Ahead
inject.description: The security team brought on DenSecure™ for threat emulation against known threat actor behavior. The team has implemented new detections that caught the attacker's persistence actions within the network.
inject.notes: The Incident Captain must reveal the Persistence card.

inject.name: Cloud Security Training
inject.description: Your security engineers downloaded Stratus Red Team and have simulated dozens of attacks in a controlled setting. They identified gaps in their current Detections and made improvements. The Defenders get a +3 modifier for the Cloud Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) Log Analysis card for the remainder of the session.

inject.name: Product Trials and Tribulation
inject.description: Your marketing team is demoing a new piece of software without letting the security group know. Your EDR lights up like a Christmas tree with unusual activity, slowing its analysis to a crawl.
inject.notes: Endpoint Security Protection Analysis is unavailable for the next 3 turns.

inject.name: Undocumented System
inject.description: That asset management and discovery project probably shouldn't have been put on hold. An undocumented system was just found on the enterprise domain and we don't really know anything about it. Who knows when this thing was spun up and for what?
inject.notes: The machine had 200 Bitcoin from 2010. The Defenders order pizza and discuss if they're going to tell management or not.

inject.name: Water, Water Everywhere!
inject.description: A pipe bursts in the server room. Seems like a good time to model that new flower print bathing suit while the backup site is brought online.
inject.notes: The Defenders receive a -3 modifier for the next two turns.

inject.name: Instance Metadata Service Version 2 (IMDSv2) Project Complete
inject.description: Your security engineers completed a year-long project that removed all use of IMDSv1 in your environment, eliminating the chance that a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) can be used to gain access to cloud credentials. The Incident Captain must reveal the Pivot and Escalate card while eating a celebratory slice of New York pizza.

inject.name: Sneaky Sneaky RAT
inject.description: The attackers gain a foothold in the environment via remote access trojan (RAT). Now they're using it to load in external files and tools to further their reach. If this isn't under control soon, you'll have more than just RATs to worry about.
inject.notes: Have the Incident Captain pull another set of Attack Cards. The Defenders get five extra turns.

inject.name: Timber!
inject.description: A tree falls and knocks out power to your office -- time to head to a secondary location. Unfortunately, traffic is terrible and you'll be stuck in the car for a while.
inject.notes: The Defender who rolled the die and caused this Inject can't help the team for three turns while they're stuck in traffic.

inject.name: It's a Feature, not a Bug
inject.description: A penetration test reveals a critical severity issue in one of your core technologies that the vendor claims is a feature, not a bug. The Defenders implement their own defenses to mitigate exploitation.
inject.notes: The Defenders receive a +2 modifier on all Procedure cards for the rest of the session.

inject.name: Supply Chain Firewall
inject.description: Your team has introduced the supply chain firewall into all developer and continuous integration (CI) workstreams reducing the likelihood that one of your developers can be compromised by a supply chain attack. The Incident Captain must reveal the Persistence card.

inject.name: Dude...Where's My Server?
inject.description: Your organization's users contact the helpdesk saying all of their fileshares are missing. Security footage reveals an unknown person absconding with the physical drives.
inject.notes: Server Analysis is unavailable to the Defenders for the rest of the session -- in addition, they lose 1 turn as they figure out whose problem this is.

inject.name: Public Storage Bucket Exposed
inject.description: A cloud storage service was misconfigured to allow public access. The bucket contained Personally Identifiable Information (PII) for thousands of your customers. The Defenders must play their Crisis Management Detection. If they are successful, they can move past this issue. If they aren't, they receive a -2 modifier on all detections for the rest of the session.

inject.name: Executive Buy-In
inject.description: An at-home PC compromise has your CEO's personally identifiable information (PII) all over the web. Suddenly, management cares a lot about security and has approved all of the team's training requests.
inject.notes: The Defenders receive a +2 modifier on all Procedure cards for the rest of the session.

inject.name: Exposed Sofware as a Service (SaaS) Application Programming Interface (API) Key During Public Presentation
inject.description: One of your engineers just gave an amazing presentation, sharing an epic story about how your company uses a SaaS product. Unfortunately, they forgot to redact their SaaS API key. Members of the audience quickly logged in and accessed your company resources. Accidents happen, but what do you do when someone exposes your organization inadvertently? The Incident Captain must draw an additional Pivot and Escalate card.

inject.name: Third-Party Code Library Compromised
inject.description: Your developer proactively ran GuardDog Command Line Interface (CLI) scans on a Python package before using it, and flagged the package as malicious, thereby avoiding a compromise. This encouraged more developers in your organization to also use GuardDog before integrating new packages into their software. The Defenders get a +3 modifier for the Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) card for the remainder of the session.

inject.name: Unexpected PLC State Change
inject.description: A programmable logic controller (PLC) has exhibited an unexpected start/stop state change. This indicates the attackers are currently active.
inject.notes: The Defenders receive a +2 modifier for Protocol Analysis on their next turn for knowing where to look.

inject.name: Safety Instrumented System (SIS) Tampering
inject.description: A safety instrumented system (SIS) goes offline, and when the maintenance crew examines it, the firmware checksum does not match.
inject.notes: The Defenders receive a +2 modifier for Endpoint Analysis on their next turn for knowing where to look.

inject.name: Mediation
inject.description: The Defenders have to function as mediators between the IT and ICS network teams.
inject.notes: All future turns receive a -1 modifier until they reveal an Attack Card, then all turns thereafter receive a +1 modifier for the goodwill period.

inject.name: You Can't Get There From Here
inject.description: Due to the remote location and travel logistics, the Defenders have to walk a site operator through the evidence collection process.
inject.notes: They receive a -1 modifier on Endpoint Analysis and Memory Analysis for the rest of the session.

inject.name: Emergency Facility Shutdown
inject.description: A compromise of a hazardous material container causes an immediate evacuation of the production facility. This is where all of the backbone ICS routers are located.
inject.notes: The Defenders lose 1 turn.

inject.name: Legacy Knowledge
inject.description: The Defenders must roll again to see if the person who built the system is still working at the site.
inject.notes: (1-10) means the happily retired individual is not there to assist them. -2 modifier on the next turn (11-20) means the grizzled veteran that deployed the legacy system still works at the site to assist them. +2 modifier on the next turn

inject.name: No High Availability (HA) System
inject.description: Current endpoint investigations are on fragile systems that are without redundancy.
inject.notes: The Defenders are limited to collecting information with the tools already installed. They receive a -2 modifier on Endpoint Analysis and Memory Analysis for the next two turns.

inject.name: No Shirt, No Shoes...
inject.description: Half of the Defenders have been deemed to be wearing inadequate personal protective equipment (PPE). They may not enter the site until they acquire full leather uppers and cotton clothes.
inject.notes: The Defenders may elect to receive a -4 modifier on their next turn OR lose 1 turn and receive a +4 modifier on the turn thereafter.

inject.name: USB Worm
inject.description: The USB devices used for collecting information become infected with autorun malware.
inject.notes: The Defenders receive a -2 modifier on Endpoint Analysis and Memory Analysis for the next two turns.

consultant.quote: "The threats are worse than you realize but not as bad as you would like to imagine." — Robert M. Lee

consultant.name: SEANbot
consultant.description: The Defenders choose between one and three turns and receive a +3 modifier but also lose that number of turns

procedure.name: Server Analysis
procedure.description: The Defenders monitor server activity, logs, and configurations to detect abnormal behaviors, such as unauthorized access, unusual traffic, or process anomalies.

procedure.name: Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) Log Analysis
procedure.description: The Defenders use SIEM to aggregate logs from systems and devices to identify abnormal patterns, such as unusual access, traffic, or attack signatures.

procedure.name: Firewall Log Analysis
procedure.description: The Defenders analyze logs generated by the firewall to monitor network traffic patterns, detect unauthorized access, and identify anomalies such as unusual connections or high traffic volumes.

procedure.name: Network Threat Hunting
procedure.description: The Defenders analyze network traffic to actively hunt for signs of malicious activity, such as unusual protocols, C2 communication, or data exfil.

procedure.name: Active Defense and Cyber Deception
procedure.description: The Defenders simulate real systems and services, luring attackers to interact with them, carefully monitoring and alerting on those interactions.

procedure.name: Endpoint Security Protection Analysis
procedure.description: The Defenders deploy and monitor endpoint security solutions to detect and prevent unauthorized access and activity on endpoints.

procedure.name: User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA)
procedure.description: The Defenders leverage advanced analytics to detect anomalies in user behavior, identifying potential insider threats, compromised accounts, or unusual activity patterns.

procedure.name: Endpoint Analysis
procedure.description: The Defenders investigate endpoint devices to identify indicators of compromise, unauthorized changes, or suspicious activities.

procedure.name: Isolation
procedure.description: The Defenders quarantine compromised systems or network segments to prevent further spread of malicious activity, containing threats while enabling secure investigation and remediation.

procedure.name: Crisis Management
procedure.description: The Defenders coordinate response efforts during cybersecurity incidents, ensuring effective communication and swift containment.

procedure.name: Memory Analysis
procedure.description: The Defenders pull the memory from the suspect system and review it for possible malicious activity, such as running malware, hidden processes, or unauthorized code execution.

procedure.name: Cloud Event Log Analysis
procedure.description: The Defenders monitor, collect, and examine event logs generated by cloud-based systems and services to identify potential security incidents, misconfigurations, and unusual or unauthorized activities.

procedure.name: Permissions Audit
procedure.description: The Defenders examine configurations such as Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles in Microsoft Active Directory, Amazon Web Services (AWS), Azure AD permissions, or file access controls to detect excessive privileges, unauthorized access, or potential insider threats.

procedure.name: Call a Consultant
procedure.description: Do you want help? Feeling stuck? Rolling badly? Need a different perspective on the incident? Then maybe it's time to phone a friend. You can choose one Consultant Card to help your team with the incident. The Consultant Card's modifier is effective immediately.

procedure.name: Physical Security Review
procedure.description: Do you have security cameras? Do you have security guards? Do you have access badges for certain areas in your facilities? Can just anyone access your sensitive IT infrastructure? No? Are you sure?

inject.name: False Alarm: It Was a Penetration Test
inject.description: Relax, it wasn't an APT, or any T for that matter — It was the External Pentesting firm the Defenders' CEO hired. They've breached everything, and now the Defenders are paying them to be told how bad it was. The Incident Captain ends the session and the Defenders discuss how they would have detected the Attack Techniques and Procedures of the Penetration Testers.

inject.name: Data Uploaded to Pastebin
inject.description: Surprise! The attackers spilled sensitive customer data all over Pastebin. Now customers are learning about the breach over their morning coffee... from The News. The Defenders must play their Crisis Management Detection. If they are successful, they can move past this issue. If they aren't, they receive a -2 modifier on all Detections for the rest of the session.

inject.name: Analyst Returns from Incident Response Training
inject.description: Armed with newfound Splunk-fu, the Defenders' Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) analyst is now a log-sifting ninja. Attackers, beware! The regex game just leveled up. The Defenders get a +2 modifier for all Detections until the end of the session.

inject.name: Policy? What Policy?
inject.description: Oops, that Detection just vanished faster than the Defenders' budget during Q4. Good luck explaining this one! The Incident Captain must remove a Detection Card.

inject.name: Luck of The SOC
inject.description: Congrats! The Defenders hit the Detection Roulette Jackpot. Let's hope it's more useful than a phishing awareness poster. The Incident Captain must reveal one of the Attack Cards.

inject.name: Bobby the Intern Kills the System You are Reviewing
inject.description: In a bold move of intern ingenuity, Bobby decides "reboot" means "unplug everything." The Defenders' investigation is now as dead as the server. The Defenders lose their next turn.

inject.name: Legal takes Your Most Skilled Handler into a Meeting to Explain the Incident
inject.description: Who brought a lawyer to the party? There's always one person who pretty much runs the whole IR process — that "One Essential Person." Well, the legal team just took that person away for "Very Important Reasons." The Defenders lose the +3 modifier on Established Detections for 2 turns.

inject.name: Missed Payday
inject.description: The attackers compromise your email account, email HR, and instruct them to update your direct deposit information, routing your paycheck into a bank account they control.
inject.notes: Each of the Defenders must roll a D20 and the person with the lowest number has to get a night job as a bartender and must remain silent for the rest of the session.

inject.name: Not a Red Team
inject.description: The network threat-hunting team has detected C2 beacons on multiple machines in your environment. The attackers can now install additional payloads on the affected machines.
inject.notes: Have the Incident Captain draw an additional Persistence Card as well as a Pivot and Escalate Card.

inject.name: Deez Registry Keyz Plz?
inject.description: A wild malicious registry key appears. The bad news: It is on 50 endpoints that are now rampant with malware. The good news: Management cares.
inject.notes: The Defenders get 3 additional turns to help solve the incident and a Consultant Card of their choice without rolling a D20.

inject.name: Nuclear Test Site
inject.description: Thank goodness the Defenders are Atomic Red Team™ power users and they are prepared for all the endpoint threats.
inject.notes: The Defenders receive a +2 modifier on Endpoint Analysis and Endpoint Security Protection Analysis for the rest of the session.

inject.name: Quishing
inject.description: The local burger joint uses a QR code for its menu. How convenient! Unfortunately, a disgruntled ex-analyst knows the Defenders are regulars and put a malicious QR code over the legitimate one. Anyone who scanned it compromised their MFA device, which now needs to be wiped or replaced.
inject.notes: The Endpoint Security Protection Analysis card is unavailable for the next two turns.

inject.name: Cat on Keyboard Deletes Production Database
inject.description: Curiosity killed the database entries! A work-from-home administrator left their computer unlocked and, in an attempt to gain additional snuggles, their cat happened to spam out a mass delete on their keyboard. Oops.
inject.notes: Each of the Defenders must roll a D20. The first two people to roll an odd number have to go fix the database and must remain silent for the rest of the session. Even number rollers move on to finish the incident.

inject.name: Undocumented System
inject.description: That asset management and discovery project probably shouldn't have been put on hold. An undocumented system was just found on the enterprise domain and we don't really know anything about it. Who knows when this thing was spun up and for what?
inject.notes: The machine had 200 Bitcoin from 2010. The Defenders order pizza and discuss if they're going to tell management or not.

inject.name: Sneaky Sneaky RAT
inject.description: The attackers gain a foothold in the environment via remote access trojan (RAT). Now they're using it to load in external files and tools to further their reach. If this isn't under control soon, you'll have more than just RATs to worry about.
inject.notes: Have the Incident Captain pull another set of Attack Cards. The Defenders get five extra turns.

procedure.name: Server Analysis
procedure.description: The Defenders monitor server activity, logs, and configurations to detect abnormal behaviors, such as unauthorized access, unusual traffic, or process anomalies.

procedure.name: Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) Log Analysis
procedure.description: The Defenders use SIEM to aggregate logs from systems and devices to identify abnormal patterns, such as unusual access, traffic, or attack signatures.

procedure.name: Firewall Log Analysis
procedure.description: The Defenders analyze logs generated by the firewall to monitor network traffic patterns, detect unauthorized access, and identify anomalies such as unusual connections or high traffic volumes.

procedure.name: Network Threat Hunting
procedure.description: The Defenders analyze network traffic to actively hunt for signs of malicious activity, such as unusual protocols, C2 communication, or data exfil.

procedure.name: Active Defense and Cyber Deception
procedure.description: The Defenders simulate real systems and services, luring attackers to interact with them, carefully monitoring and alerting on those interactions.

procedure.name: Endpoint Security Protection Analysis
procedure.description: The Defenders deploy and monitor endpoint security solutions to detect and prevent unauthorized access and activity on endpoints.

procedure.name: User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA)
procedure.description: The Defenders leverage advanced analytics to detect anomalies in user behavior, identifying potential insider threats, compromised accounts, or unusual activity patterns.

procedure.name: Endpoint Analysis
procedure.description: The Defenders investigate endpoint devices to identify indicators of compromise, unauthorized changes, or suspicious activities.

procedure.name: Isolation
procedure.description: The Defenders quarantine compromised systems or network segments to prevent further spread of malicious activity, containing threats while enabling secure investigation and remediation.

procedure.name: Crisis Management
procedure.description: The Defenders coordinate response efforts during cybersecurity incidents, ensuring effective communication and swift containment.

procedure.name: Memory Analysis
procedure.description: The Defenders pull the memory from the suspect system and review it for possible malicious activity, such as running malware, hidden processes, or unauthorized code execution.

procedure.name: Cloud Event Log Analysis
procedure.description: The Defenders monitor, collect, and examine event logs generated by cloud-based systems and services to identify potential security incidents, misconfigurations, and unusual or unauthorized activities.

procedure.name: Permissions Audit
procedure.description: The Defenders examine configurations such as Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles in Microsoft Active Directory, Amazon Web Services (AWS), Azure AD permissions, or file access controls to detect excessive privileges, unauthorized access, or potential insider threats.

procedure.name: Cloud Event Log Analysis
procedure.description: Are you missing what should be in your cloud logs? Do you even know what cloud provider logs you need in an incident response situation? There are thousands of data connectors in your cloud service provider. Have any of them changed since the last time you reviewed them? Good luck hunting for a specific needle in a stack of needles.
tools: Check with your cloud provider and see what tools they provide. It's ok, you're paying them a ton of money for all this.

procedure.name: Permissions Audit
procedure.description: Users can have everything by default... which makes your organization vulnerable by design. Who gets to do what and why? Who is the magical unicorn that gets the exceptions? Are permissions open for convenience? When was the last time you fixed something a security audit didn't make you do? You can be the decider if you want--the power is yours!

procedure.name: Call a Consultant
procedure.description: Do you want help? Feeling stuck? Rolling badly? Need a different perspective on the incident? Then maybe it's time to phone a friend. You can choose one Consultant Card to help your team with the incident. The Consultant Card's modifier is effective immediately.

inject.name: False Alarm: It Was a Penetration Test
inject.description: Relax, it wasn't an APT, or any T for that matter — It was the External Pentesting firm the Defenders' CEO hired. They've breached everything, and now the Defenders are paying them to be told how bad it was. The Incident Captain ends the session and the Defenders discuss how they would have detected the Attack Techniques and Procedures of the Penetration Testers.

inject.name: Data Uploaded to Pastebin
inject.description: Surprise! The attackers spilled sensitive customer data all over Pastebin. Now customers are learning about the breach over their morning coffee... from The News. The Defenders must play their Crisis Management Detection. If they are successful, they can move past this issue. If they aren't, they receive a -2 modifier on all Detections for the rest of the session.

inject.name: Analyst Returns from Incident Response Training
inject.description: Armed with newfound Splunk-fu, the Defenders' Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) analyst is now a log-sifting ninja. Attackers, beware! The regex game just leveled up. The Defenders get a +2 modifier for all Detections until the end of the session.

inject.name: Policy? What Policy?
inject.description: Oops, that Detection just vanished faster than the Defenders' budget during Q4. Good luck explaining this one! The Incident Captain must remove a Detection Card.

inject.name: Luck of The SOC
inject.description: Congrats! The Defenders hit the Detection Roulette Jackpot. Let's hope it's more useful than a phishing awareness poster. The Incident Captain must reveal one of the Attack Cards.

inject.name: Bobby the Intern Kills the System You are Reviewing
inject.description: In a bold move of intern ingenuity, Bobby decides "reboot" means "unplug everything." The Defenders' investigation is now as dead as the server. The Defenders lose their next turn.

inject.name: Legal takes Your Most Skilled Handler into a Meeting to Explain the Incident
inject.description: Who brought a lawyer to the party? There's always one person who pretty much runs the whole IR process — that "One Essential Person." Well, the legal team just took that person away for "Very Important Reasons." The Defenders lose the +3 modifier on Established Detections for 2 turns.

inject.name: Bear vs. Powerstation
inject.description: A bear attacked the power substation for your datacenter. Don't worry, he's down, but so is your datacenter. The only thing worse than the smell is not having a hot backup facility.
inject.notes: The defenders lose 1 turn as they discuss the difference between a hot backup and a cold backup.

inject.name: Ghosted by AV
inject.description: A recent unverified update caused all endpoints to alarm on false positives. A useless antivirus is as good as no AV at all. Do you shut it down or keep it running while sifting through all the noise?
inject.notes: The Defenders receive a -3 modifier on Endpoint Security Protection Analysis for the rest of the session.

inject.name: DiscountConsultant.lol
inject.description: Ever since hiring Scott, this incident response has gone from bad to worse. He had us chasing the wrong lead the whole time. Turns out, our consultant has no real IR experience despite a senior title. Luckily, he has red team experience and recognizes the TTPs.
inject.notes: The Defenders must roll a die. If the die is even, the Incident Captain must reveal the Initial Compromise card. If the die is odd, the Incident Captain must draw another Persistence card.

inject.name: Trimarc123!
inject.description: The attackers' access to your network just fell into their laps. The local admin account on all workstations share the same password, so if the attackers gained admin on one workstation, they can now log in to them all.
inject.notes: If one of the Defenders can accurately explain LAPS, the Incident Captain must reveal the Pivot & Escalate card. Otherwise, the Incident Captain must draw an additional Pivot & Escalate card.

inject.name: Dude, Where's Our Docs?
inject.description: The project to fully document important incident response procedures was not started on time and never finished.
inject.notes: The Defenders no longer have a +3 modifier on their Established Procedure cards.

inject.name: Click, Click, Boom
inject.description: Instead of buying new hard drives, you decided to save some money on "refurbished" drives. Don't worry, you didn't use those drives on anything important -- only your SIEM -- ya know, that system you spend all that money on and don't use.
inject.notes: SIEM Log Analysis is unavailable to the Defenders for the rest of the session.

inject.name: Peekaboo
inject.description: Remember that DIY security camera you set up to keep an eye on your servers? Well, you forgot to secure it and change the default password, so now the bad guys know all of your secrets.
inject.notes: The Incident Captain must draw an additional Initial Compromise card.

inject.name: Product Trials and Tribulation
inject.description: Your marketing team is demoing a new piece of software without letting the security group know. Your EDR lights up like a Christmas tree with unusual activity, slowing its analysis to a crawl.
inject.notes: Endpoint Security Protection Analysis is unavailable for the next 3 turns.

consultant.name: Jake Hildreth
consultant.description: The Defenders get an extra (3) turns to complete the session
consultant.quote: "We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit." — Will Durant

consultant.name: Dev Badlu
consultant.description: The Defenders must reveal the C2 and Exfil card
specialties: Building Tools to Help Combat Human Trafficking
consultant.quote: "Security is like an onion, the more layers you have the more crying the red team is going to be doing." — Dev

consultant.name: Sean Metcalf
consultant.description: The Defenders choose any one of the scenario cards to be revealed
consultant.quote: "The question every organization has to answer for themselves is do they want to take the red pill & learn their security issues or the blue pill and continue thinking everything is fine." — Sean

consultant.name: Brandon Colley
consultant.description: The Defenders get to choose an additional (2) Consultant Cards
consultant.quote: "Make a decision, even if it’s wrong." — Dad

consultant.name: SEANbot
consultant.description: The Defenders choose between one and three turns and receive a +3 modifier but also lose that number of turns
